text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government is working on a new plan to clamp down on widespread tax evasion.
- The two rival leftist parties in parliament say they can work together to oppose the Islamist-led government they believe is endangering the secularist state.
- The powerful national security council is to investigate the purchase of pump-action guns by radical Islamist groups.
- French and U.S. firms are queuing up to enter Turkey's lucrative mobile telephone market.

- A leftist party wants is seeking high penalties against couples who marry only with a religious ceremony. Moslem wedding ceremonies are condoned in Turkey but couples must also have an official ceremony for their marriage to be valid.
- Turkey is cracking under the weight of its huge foreign and domestic debt mountain with no way out in sight.

- President Suleyman Demirel discussed various formulae for coalition governments in parliament when he visited party offices to celebrate the Moslem Eid al-Fitr festival. The Islamist-led government faces a censure motion from opposition parties this month.
